classification.difficultyReason: Transfer an angle along a parallel ray and use the marked right angle to find the second angle.

spec.description: Unlettered triangle with its left side extended upwards and a parallel upward ray at the lower-right vertex. Matching chevrons mark the upward arms. The upper triangle angle is 33 degrees; the lower-right right angle is partitioned into x and y. Only the three triangle vertices have point markers.
spec.mathematics: Internal coordinate aliases L, U and R are not printed. LU is parallel to the ray from R; LR is perpendicular to that ray. LU=2/tan(33 degrees) and LR=2 in internal drawing units, so angle LUR=33 degrees, x=33 degrees and y=57 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: 33 degrees, x degrees and y degrees are visible. Neither computed unknown is printed.

answer.worked:
$x=33^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}x+y&=90^\circ\\33^\circ+y&=90^\circ\\y&=57^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles in a right angle.
